findings.how_to_check: Run MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do to inspect the 436 discrepancy pairs in MATCHING/results/tgt_fallback_diag.md. Run MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do and confirm it aborts with error 459 at line 130.
findings.suggested_fix: Use tgt_fallback_diag.md to identify the source of discrepancy between the two cleaning paths (e.g. whitespace or suffix normalization differences), harmonize the upstream cleaning or select the authoritative fallback, and verify nbad==0 before rerunning the pipeline.
findings.title: The target-only builder still exits on 436 known fallback inconsistencies
findings.what_the_code_does: The builder counts records satisfying `name_true_cleaned_exists==0 & !(f_name==f_ans & l_name==l_ans)` into `nbad` and halts with `exit 459` whenever `nbad>0`. The brief documents that current data produces `nbad==436`. While `tgt_fallback_diag.do` profiles these records, `1c_tgt_divided_files.do` itself has not been changed to resolve the discrepancies, so rerunning the pipeline will still abort at line 130.
findings.why_it_matters: The target-only linkage run cannot complete to generate the counterfactual link files. Resolving the discrepancies by simply dropping the check would be unsafe because differing name strings affect candidate linkage and match uniqueness.

findings.how_to_check: Examine the diagnostic output from tgt_fallback_diag.do for the age and birthplace distribution of the 4.8M unmatched records. Run linkage sensitivity checks treating this group under alternative rules (e.g. model names vs. Ancestry fallback) and evaluate changes in match rates and precision.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly document the handling of records absent from census1940_all_labeled_data.dta in the paper/slides. Perform a sensitivity check showing whether retaining Ancestry names versus applying model names to this group materially affects the resulting linkage distribution.
findings.title: Millions of records without measured target status are assigned to the non-target group
findings.what_the_code_does: Target status is derived solely from `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` via `tgt = !(namefrst==namefrst_fs & namelast==namelast_fs)`. Divided-file records unmatched to the target flag receive `tgt=0` at line 101, combining observed commercial agreements with 4,819,575 records absent from the labeled dataset (which excludes records with blank names or missing ages in either commercial source).
findings.why_it_matters: For these 4.8 million records, commercial transcription agreement has not been confirmed. Coding them as non-targets forces Ancestry names rather than model names. Through candidate competition in the ABE matching algorithm, this affects match rates and link composition for both these records and others, creating potential selection bias in the purported target-only counterfactual.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied; claims-vs-code review was limited to assertions and comments in the modified scripts and review briefs.
External census and divided-file datasets ($REP_F and $REP_SNU) reside outside the repository and are gitignored; runtime execution could not be performed.
Diff-scoped review of uncommitted working tree and untracked files as reported by git status --short, not a full-repository audit.
structured_output.summary: The target-only flag optimization in 1c_tgt_divided_files.do preserves record-level target assignments while substantially reducing merge overhead, and the revised diagnostic correctly queries the full census ID universe and guards empty results. However, the production pipeline is still blocked by 436 known fallback name discrepancies where 1c_tgt_divided_files.do halts on assertion error 459. Furthermore, 4.8 million records lacking Ancestry–FamilySearch agreement status are silently coded as non-targets, an identification choice that should be evaluated for sensitivity in candidate competition.

verified_clean.item: Target flag shrinkage preserves exact record-level assignments

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
